observations: A broad yellow rectangle frames the composition on three sides, enclosing a dense grid of smaller rectangles stacked vertically to suggest a face structure.

Three tightly wound spiral forms appear across the upper and middle zones — one in the upper-left panel, one large central spiral, and one in the upper-right panel — each layered in yellow, red, blue, and black rings.
A horizontal band near the lower third contains a zigzag black line running across a pink and white field, flanked above and below by thick yellow borders, reading as a tooth-filled mouth.
reading: Yellow scaffolding holds the face structure together like a frame within a frame, while three spirals pull the eye inward at different depths. The zigzag mouth band sits flat and wide, more mechanical than expressive. A small red loop at the left edge sits apart from the main structure, quieter than the surrounding density. The image reads as confrontational — more like a fixed stare than an outburst.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #34 and #36. Where #34 fills a rounded form with loose overlapping lines on white, #35 locks its face inside a hard yellow grid on a dark ground, trading organic sprawl for rigid compartments.

connections.reason: Both #35 and #36 use concentric ring eyes set inside rectangular panels, but #36 places them against a dark brown ground with far less surrounding line density, so the spiral forms read in isolation rather than as part of a packed grid.

nnotb #4 shares a concentric-ring form embedded in a dense rectangular field with a wavy border, offering a cross-collection comparison of how a spiral-and-grid structure appears outside the owned nifty-faces subset.

lookingQuestion: The three spiral forms differ in size and sit in separate panels — what does the variation in their scale and surrounding color do to how your eye moves between them?
ambiguities: The small red loop at the left edge is visually distinct from the main face structure; whether it functions as a separate eye element, a mark, or incidental line work cannot be determined from the image alone.
Title-derived order and recorded-creation order align here, but the metadata notes gaps and variants exist across the full series, so adjacency does not confirm sequential making.
